trainingPlans.name: 30-Minute 5K Treadmill Progression
trainingPlans.source: Full treadmill progression from the July 2026 return-to-running starter week through a target continuous 5 km in approximately 30 minutes by mid-November 2026. Historical sessions are retained for reference.

goal.primaryGoal: Run 5 km continuously on the treadmill in approximately 30 minutes by mid-November 2026.

checkpoints.target: Progress to 5 x 3 minute running intervals at 7.0 km/h.
Complete 2 x 10 min running at 7.5 km/h with a short walking recovery.
Run continuously for 25 minutes at an easy controlled effort.
Accumulate 18 minutes of running at 10.0 km/h.
Accumulate 24 minutes of running at 10.0 km/h.
Run 5 km continuously in approximately 30 minutes.

phases.name: Starter Return to Running
phases.focus: Reintroduce running impact conservatively after the layoff using short run-walk intervals.

phases.name: Early Run-Walk Progression
phases.focus: Gradually increase individual running intervals from 90 seconds to 3 minutes while keeping pace controlled.

phases.name: Extend Running Intervals
phases.focus: Increase the duration of each running interval without chasing speed.

phases.name: Build Continuous Running
phases.focus: Reduce walking recoveries and progress toward 30 minutes of continuous easy running.

phases.name: Develop 5K Pace
phases.focus: Maintain continuous running ability while progressively introducing faster running toward 10.0 km/h.

phases.name: 5K Specific
phases.focus: Increase time spent at target pace, reduce fatigue and attempt the 30-minute 5K.

readinessRules: Every treadmill workout must be scheduled in the Morning slot.
Pre-Run Dynamic Mobility must be scheduled in the same Morning slot as every treadmill workout.
Pre-Run Dynamic Mobility should be completed immediately before the treadmill session.
Use 0.5% treadmill incline unless there is a specific reason not to.
Do not make up a missed treadmill session by adding it to another day.
If a progression session cannot be completed with controlled running form, repeat that stage rather than progressing.
Easy and continuous sessions should remain conversational and controlled rather than becoming time trials.
Walking recoveries can remain walking until jogging them feels genuinely easy.
Do not increase the prescribed speed of goal-pace sessions simply because the session feels good.
After the cruise, stag weekend and wedding, prioritise re-entry and consistency rather than trying to recover missed training.
If the 30-minute 5K is not achieved on 11 November, complete the 5 km continuously if possible, record the result and use that performance to guide the next progression.
